title: Streaming accounting gap on resume after prolonged idle across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers escalated unexpected under-reporting of streamed token usage after long idle periods followed by a resume of the stream. Affected environments: Hosted API, Dedicated pools during failover, and Private deployments using legacy ingress. Symptoms: token counts in customer dashboards are lower than actual application-side counts; resulting in corrective credits and billing adjustments. Initial reports surfaced 2026-03-09 and escalated via CSMs for 3 enterprise customers (cust-224, cust-311, cust-477).
impact: Multiple customers experienced underbilling (customer-visible), finance team saw negative adjustments when reconciling; estimated cross-tenant undercount between 0.3% and 2.1% of streaming tokens for impacted windows. High business impact for customers on committed/dedicated plans and those with strict observability requirements.
detection_timeline: 2026-03-09: First customer support ticket (cust-224) reporting tokens missing from hour-level dashboards. 2026-03-10: Pager alert from billing-reconcile job for negative delta on hosted invoices. 2026-03-10 evening: Correlated with recent dedicated node failover where streaming sessions were handed off. 2026-03-11: Confirmed reproduction in staging with a crafted client that pauses a stream for >30s then resumes.
root_cause_summary: A bug in the streaming request aggregator that handles partial chunk accounting across connection handoffs. When a client pauses and resumes a stream, the aggregator's ephemeral partial-token buffer was not persisted across the session rebind step performed during dedicated failovers and in our legacy private ingress path. The last in-flight chunk that contained token counters was dropped from the durable accounting record. The runtime still delivered bytes to the client (no functional failure), but the metering aggregation pipeline never received the final partial-chunk accounting event, producing undercounted tokens.
technical_findings:
- The issue occurs on both HTTP/1.1 chunked and HTTP/2 streaming paths.
- Reproducer: open streaming request, send tokens, pause >30s, then send more tokens; metering counter misses the pre-pause partial count unless the session persists buffer.
- Failure triggered during (A) dedicated node handoff (session rebind) and (B) private ingress path when the connection was proxied by legacy gateway which dropped the 'partial_token_buffer' header.
- Metering pipeline expects final chunk events with 'accumulated_token_delta' and was not tolerant of missing final fragments.
- Existing unit-tests did not cover pause/resume semantics nor ingress rebind scenarios.
mitigation_and_workaround: 1) Hotfix deployed to hosted runtime nodes (runtime-1.19.3-hotfix) on 2026-03-11: persist partial-token buffer into the session metadata before any handoff, and emit a synthetic final-accounting event when a handoff completes. 2) For Dedicated customers: ops ran a targeted rolling patch to pool controllers to avoid drop during planned failovers. 3) For Private: customer-facing workaround documented (enable 'session-pinning' on ingress or upgrade ingress to gateway-2.4+).
permanent_fix_plan:
- Merge PR #1289 that centralizes partial-chunk accounting into the durable request-store and guarantees emission of final accounting events even if the connection is terminated or re-bound.
- Add e2e streaming pause/resume tests across HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 in the integration suite.
- Deploy runtime release runtime-1.20 (includes the PR and additional logging) to Hosted and Dedicated by 2026-03-20, and produce a Private package (private-runtime-1.20) for customer upgrades.
backfill_and_reconciliation:
- Implemented a reconciliation job 'streaming-resume-reconcile-v1' to scan raw ingress event logs and reconstruct missing token deltas for windows between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-11.
- Backfill run id: brf-20260312-07; run produced candidate adjustments for 8 customers.
- Finance approved automated crediting for customers with confirmed undercount > 0.5%. Manual review for others.
customer_communication:
- 2026-03-12: Sent targeted emails to affected customers with timeline, explanation, and expected credits.
- Posted status update in the dashboard incidents pane and notified CSMs.
- For Dedicated customers, engaged SEs for coordinated patch windows.
actions_taken:
- Hotfix applied to hosted clusters (runtime-1.19.3-hotfix) and verified against reproducer.
- Backfill job executed and finance credits scheduled.
- PR #1289 opened and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289.
- Confluence incident writeup: https://confluence.redwood/incident/2026-03-streaming-accounting-gap.
- Monitoring: added metric 'streaming.partial_chunk_drops' and an alert when >0.1% of streams emit a drop.
next_steps:
- Complete PR code review and merge by 2026-03-14.
- Deploy runtime-1.20 to staging and run integration tests (target 2026-03-17).
- Schedule Dedicated production rollout (coordinated maintenance windows) and publish Private upgrade notes by 2026-03-20.
- Improve billing reconciliation dashboards to surface negative deltas earlier and add a weekly audit job for streaming pathways.
